{"body":"## Feature Request

Both the tree-local and cross-tree member search only match a single substring against `first_name`, `last_name`, and `maiden_name` independently (`member_name_search_clause` in `backend/app/services/member_search.py`, used by `backend/app/api/routes/search.py` and the in-tree search). A multi-word query like `"Anna Müller 1932"` or `"Müller Anna"` is matched as one literal substring, so it only finds a hit if the stored name happens to contain that exact sequence — it does not, for example, match a member with `first_name="Anna"`, `last_name="Müller"`, `date_of_birth` in 1932 when the words are typed in a different order or combined with a date.

## Expected Behavior

Extend name search so a multi-token query is split and matched more flexibly:

- Recognize common permutations: `"First Last"` and `"Last First"` should both match a member regardless of which field holds which token.
- Recognize a trailing/leading year or full date token (e.g. `"Anna Müller 1932"`, `"1932 Anna"`) and match it against `date_of_birth`/`date_of_birth_sort` (and possibly `date_of_death`) in addition to the name tokens.
- Each token should still be matched independently (AND across tokens, not requiring the exact substring), so `"Anna Müller"` matches regardless of whitespace/order between the two name fields.
- First or Lastname should also match partial: Müller Ann or Anna Mü

Out of scope for this issue: typo-tolerant / fuzzy matching (e.g. Levenshtein or trigram similarity) — that's a bigger change (new matching strategy, ranking, possibly a new Postgres extension like `pg_trgm`) and should be tracked separately if wanted.

## Suggested approach

- Update `member_name_search_clause` (and callers in `backend/app/api/routes/members.py` local search and `backend/app/api/routes/search.py` cross-tree search) to tokenize the query on whitespace, detect a year/date-like token, and build an AND of per-token OR clauses across `first_name`/`last_name`/`maiden_name` (plus the date columns for date-like tokens) instead of one big substring match.
- Keep it index/DB-friendly (still using `ilike`), since this runs across potentially many trees in the cross-tree endpoint.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `"First Last"` and `"Last First"` both match the same member
- [ ] A query containing a 4-digit year matches members with that birth year, combined with a name token
- [ ] Existing single-token substring search behavior is unchanged
- [ ] Backend tests cover permutation and date-token cases for both local and cross-tree search
- [ ] `CHANGELOG.md` entry under `## [Unreleased]`

- `backend/app/api/routes/search.py`

member search currently match the **entire query as one literal substring**
against `first_name`, `last_name`, and `maiden_name` (see
`member_name_search_clause` in `backend/app/services/member_search.py`). So
`"Anna Müller"` only matches if one field literally contains that sequence — a
member with `first_name="Anna"`, `last_name="Müller"` is missed, and reversing
to `"Müller Anna"` or adding a birth year (`"Anna Müller 1932"`) never matches.

Goal: tokenize multi-word queries and match each token independently (AND across
tokens), where each token can hit any name field, and a 4-digit **year** token
additionally matches the birth/death date columns. This makes name-order
permutations and `name + year` queries work while keeping single-token behavior
byte-for-byte unchanged. Fuzzy/typo matching is explicitly out of scope.

All logic stays in `member_name_search_clause`; the two callers are untouched
because they already delegate the WHERE clause to it.

   the current `or_(first_name, last_name, maiden_name)` ilike against
   `f"%{query}%"` (use the raw `query`, not the token, to preserve exact current
   semantics incl. whitespace-only edge case).
